extracted.intended_audience: aspiring Pitch Wars applicants / emerging fiction writers seeking mentorship
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for preparing a Pitch Wars submission: polishing manuscript, writing query and synopsis, crafting an author bio, demonstrating coachability, and engaging the community to appeal to mentors and judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand What Mentors Are Seeking
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch Wars mentors are not just looking for good writing; they’re searching for stories with strong potential and writers who are open to constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research mentors carefully: read their bios, look at their wish lists, and identify who aligns with your genre and style. Tailoring your submission to their interests demonstrates homework done and gives a competitive edge (e.g., a fantasy mentor may prioritize world-building; a romance mentor may focus on emotional arcs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect Your Manuscript Before Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors expect a polished manuscript from the start; grammar errors, inconsistencies, or a weak opening can quickly disqualify your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on creating a strong hook in your opening pages. Workshop your manuscript with critique partners or beta readers to identify weak spots, improve pacing, and strengthen character development. Demonstrable effort and commitment to craft attract mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a Query Letter That Shines
rubrics_metrics.description: Your query letter is your first impression and should succinctly introduce your manuscript, highlight the stakes, and convey why your story is unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure with: a compelling opening hook; a brief summary of your story (including protagonist, conflict, and stakes); and a closing paragraph with relevant personal details (e.g., writing experience or why you’re submitting to Pitch Wars). Avoid clichés and generic pitches; personalize the query to specific mentors to increase selection chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight Your Willingness to Learn (Coachability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors want writers who are coachable and open to feedback; they’re not expecting perfection but expect eagerness to improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In submission materials emphasize a growth mindset: state willingness to revise, mention how you’ve responded to feedback previously, and express excitement to collaborate with a mentor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a Strong Synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: A synopsis gives mentors and judges a clear sense of your story and should be concise and focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the synopsis concise (1–2 pages) and concentrate on main plot points, key characters, and resolution. Avoid vague language or excessive subplots; focus on the core of the story and what makes it compelling so mentors can quickly assess fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage Your Author Bio
rubrics_metrics.description: Your author bio is an opportunity to impress; you don’t need publishing history but should share relevant experiences that add credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention writing groups, workshops, projects, or background directly tied to the manuscript (e.g., a legal background for a legal thriller). Avoid listing unrelated details unless they directly tie into your manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network and Engage with the Community
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch Wars is a community; engaging with it can provide insights and opportunities beyond the submission itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in Twitter chats, join forums, and connect with past participants to learn about experiences, stay informed about updates, and build relationships that can help during the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Common Mistakes and Follow Submission Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain procedural and stylistic errors can harm your chances regardless of story quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always follow rules for formatting, word count, and deadlines. Submit a complete, finished, polished manuscript (not incomplete). Avoid overloading your submission with gimmicks or flashy extras—focus on showcasing your story and writing. These errors signal unprofessionalism and reduce selection likelihood.
